title: I Bow to the Lord
translation: I bow to the Lord, O Ishana, whose form is liberation, the all-pervading, the embodiment of Brahman and the Vedas. I worship him who is his own self, beyond qualities, changeless and desireless, the sky of consciousness, who dwells in the sky itself.
translation_hi: हे ईशान, मैं उन ईश्वर को नमस्कार करता हूँ जो मोक्ष स्वरूप, सर्वव्यापी, ब्रह्म और वेद स्वरूप हैं। मैं उन्हें भजता हूँ जो अपने स्वरूप में स्थित, निर्गुण, निर्विकल्प, इच्छारहित, चेतना रूपी आकाश हैं और आकाश में ही निवास करते हैं।

words.note: Vocative: a name of Shiva, lord of the north-east.

words.meaning: embodiment of Brahman and the Vedas

grammar: Accusative chain: every epithet ends in -म् because each is an object of नमामि and भजे.
nir- 'without': निर्गुण, निर्विकल्प, निरीह, like निराकार in Nirvana Shatkam.
Author: Goswami Tulsidas, in the Uttarakanda of the Ramcharitmanas (16th century). The Brahmin in the story recites it to please Shiva.
